item.title: 'Dawson's Creek' actor James Van Der Beek dead at 48
item.description: James Van Der Beek, who rose to teen idol status in the show "Dawson's Creek," has died after a battle with colorectal cancer.

item.title: Garland Arts unveils two thrilling musicals this month
item.description: The Company of Rowlett Performances will present "The Musical of Musicals (The Musical!)" at the Plaza Theatre from Feb. 13 through Feb. 22, and Grace Academy of Dallas will present "Disney's Beauty and the Beast Jr." at the Granville Arts Center on Feb. 26 and Feb. 27.

item.title: Drinking 2-3 coffees a day may lower dementia risk — but not if it’s decaf
item.description: Daily coffee drinking may lower dementia risk, according to new study.

item.title: Garland Symphony Orchestra features harpist Michelle Campos
item.description: The Garland Symphony Orchestra will feature its principal harpist, Michelle Campos, in a concert at the Granville Arts Center on Feb. 13, featuring a selection of dance-themed classical works and overtures.

item.title: Rainbow Vomit to close at Fair Park after seven years
item.description: Rainbow Vomit, the immersive art experience at Fair Park in Dallas, will close its doors on March 23, 2026.

item.title: Café Olivia opens in Downtown Dallas with fresh new menu
item.description: Café Olivia is opening a new location in the Dallas Arts Tower on February 17th, featuring an expanded menu of clean ingredients and chef-driven dishes, as well as art-related programming and community engagement.

item.title: Enjoy free St. Patrick's Day festivities at the Village Dallas
item.description: The Village Dallas will host a free St. Patrick's Day celebration featuring live music, food and drink specials, and interactive games on March 14.

item.title: Original ChopShop to open new Fort Worth spot in Med District
item.description: Original ChopShop will open its newest Fort Worth location in the Medical District in late March 2026.

item.title: Texas lands in the top 10 sexiest states
item.description: According to a new survey of 4,000 Americans, Texans are feeling especially sexy this year.

item.title: Texas named one of the most deceitful states in America
item.description: Texas was ranked as the sixth most deceitful state in the US, with 22.4% of residents admitting to lying frequently, the fourth highest rate of identity theft in the country, and a high prevalence of star signs considered deceitful by the study.
